policy_title: Legislate for Annual Oil and Gas Licensing Rounds
stated: The Conservative Party will legislate to ensure annual licensing rounds for oil and gas production from the North Sea to provide energy, protect jobs, and reduce reliance on foreign powers, while keeping the windfall tax in place until 2028-29 or until prices normalize.

source.quote: We will legislate to ensure annual licensing rounds for oil and gas production from our own North Sea to provide energy to homes and businesses across the country and protect high-skilled and well-paid jobs in the industry.

bearing_set.reason: The explicit energy-security rationale — reducing reliance on foreign powers — is a genuine resilience-to-external-threats consideration that earns a real verdict on national security posture.
Annual licensing rounds for fossil-fuel extraction directly and materially bear on the UK's emissions trajectory and its credible pathway to net zero.
The policy explicitly targets job protection in the North Sea oil and gas sector, earning a real verdict on employment security for workers in that industry and its supply chain.

Sustaining annual licensing rounds affects business investment in the North Sea and near-term UK economic output, with a dual-horizon tension against long-run transition costs and stranded-asset risk — a real verdict on aggregate living standards and investment.

membership_note: Four fundamentals bear genuinely: O6 (climate/emissions, worsens), O5 (energy security/national security, improves), O4 (North Sea jobs, improves), O13 (near-term investment vs long-run transition costs, mixed/dual-horizon). Energy-price effects on O2 are plausible but marginal given global gas-market pricing; the windfall-tax retention does not materially alter O12 beyond current baseline. O9/O10/O1/O3/O7/O8 are not substantively engaged.
